row: 30000156 / OWR-768-006: Limiting Cycle Distributions of Birational Maps

A fixed birational map without a prime-field cycle-distribution limit — Alec Kriebel (ORCID 0009-0001-9320-500X), v1.1 (2026-10-21). Unrefereed preprint. Fixed L(u,v)=(u,(u²+1)v) permutes the full affine plane for p≡3 mod4; point-weighted periods normalized by p have, at each fixed 1/2≤x<1, CDF 1−φ(p−1)/(p−1)+o(1), limsup 1 and liminf at most 23/24. Neither those CDF values nor the period measures converge on any admissible prime subset of positive upper relative density. A separate all-odd-prime proposition treats the regular domain p(p-r), r=0 or2, and uniform-point exceptional-fiber deletion or arbitrary finite nonnegative assigned periods only there. Bounded statistics change by O(1/p); no positive-upper-prime-density selection restores convergence under these conventions. Completed measures lie on nonnegative reals; assigned periods may exceed p. The triangular family, primitive quadratic values, shifted-prime totient mean and continuous scalar law are established and credited; this is a scoped application to Vivaldi’s 2004 broad existence assertion (joint work with Roberts). No new map family, character-sum theorem, arithmetic mean/scalar law, universal elliptic, polynomial-automorphism or prime-average cycle theorem claimed. Bounded priority audit found no authenticated exact earlier application in inspected sources; the cited Neumärker–Roberts–Viallet–Vivaldi 2011 preprint body/version relationships remain unrecovered. No worldwide novelty, current-open status or historical firstness claim.
